note: Repository-grounded, reusable security remediation patterns. HUMAN-AUTHORED. Every 'safe' entry points at a REAL fix already merged in this repo (commit + path) so a future task reuses the proven canonical remedy instead of re-deriving it. Detection regexes power the static guards in apps/backend/test/static-injection-guards.test.ts. Not a substitute for reading source; a router uses `applies_when` to attach the right pattern to a task context bundle.

patterns.threat: Predictable or biased values used where unpredictability matters (tokens, claim keys, referral/display codes).
unsafe_patterns: Math.floor(randomByte / slot) reductions of a raw CSPRNG byte
patterns.safe_pattern: crypto.randomInt(max) for a uniform index; crypto.randomUUID() / crypto.getRandomValues() for keys. No manual byte->index arithmetic.
patterns.regression: Inject the randomness source; assert one uniform draw per char + byte-range; deterministic full-range distribution (no timing).
patterns.bypass_notes: CodeQL flags ANY arithmetic reduction of a crypto byte, even after rejection sampling — prefer crypto.randomInt over % or / entirely.

patterns.threat: Server-side HTTP to an admin/user-influenced URL reaching cloud metadata / internal hosts, incl. via redirects.
unsafe_patterns: global fetch(url) on a stored/user-influenced URL
redirect: 'follow' on such a fetch (a 302 to 169.254.169.254 defeats any pre-check)
patterns.safe_pattern: Route through OutboundHttpService.request()/requestBinary() — it applies assertAllowedOutboundUrl (scheme allowlist + metadata block), routes via the egress proxy, and does not follow redirects.
patterns.regression: Assert assertAllowedOutboundUrl rejects metadata IPv4/IPv6/GCP + non-http(s) schemes; a static no-raw-fetch guard on the fixed service.
patterns.bypass_notes: assertAllowedOutboundUrl intentionally ALLOWS localhost/private (health probes use the local egress relay) — do NOT tighten the shared policy without human review; the no-redirect + proxy boundary is what clears the alert.
applies_when: any server-side fetch of a stored URL

patterns.threat: Predictable filename in the shared os.tmpdir() enabling a local pre-create/symlink race.
patterns.safe_pattern: createSecureTempFile(basename): fs.mkdtemp('afrows-') private 0700 dir, write with mode 0o600, recursive cleanup in finally.

repo_examples.note: original mkdtemp+chmod idiom the helper mirrors

patterns.regression: Helper unit tests (path under tmpdir, 0700 dir, no collision, cleanup) + static no-predictable-tmpfile guard on the affected services.
patterns.bypass_notes: Preserve the exact basename/extension the child binary expects; keep cleanup in finally (now removes the dir).
applies_when: any temp-file handoff to a child process

patterns.threat: Polynomial regex backtracking on user-influenced input blocking the single-threaded event loop.
unsafe_patterns: unbounded input reaching the regex before any length cap
patterns.safe_pattern: Linear two-pointer character strip (stripSurroundingUnderscores) — no backtracking, byte-identical output. Splitting the alternation does NOT fix it (measured still quadratic).
patterns.regression: Full normalization contract + pathological input 'a'+'_'.repeat(50000)+'b' (completion+correctness, NOT timing) + static guard against /^_+|_+$/g.
patterns.bypass_notes: The obvious /^_+/ + /_+$/ split is a measured trap (still O(n^2)); use character scanning.
applies_when: any anchored repeated-char strip on user input

patterns.threat: User/config-influenced value interpolated into a shell command string.
unsafe_patterns: spawn/exec with a shell string built from input
patterns.safe_pattern: execFile/spawn with an ARGUMENT ARRAY (no shell); for identifiers use the command-safety sanitizers (safePathSegment, safeRouteTableName, shellToken) before interpolation.
patterns.regression: Adversarial payloads ('; rm -rf / #, $(id), a'b) asserted neutralized; prefer argument-array invocation.
patterns.bypass_notes: The open alerts #12/#13 are operator-run standalone scripts (not app-reachable) — a future grouped task, not urgent.
applies_when: any child-process invocation with interpolated input
